statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 15 sits in the low band and well below the block threshold, while Stress 46 is elevated and Confidence 88 is high.
recommendation: The deterministic mapping from Tail 15 produces EA_ON with a green status, pause false and caution false. A narrow danger window is marked from 13:30Z to 14:30Z, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00Z cluster of three medium-impact releases. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ's sixth overnight extreme at 29,290.25 fails to hold and price retraces about 60 points to 29,228.75, the first meaningful pullback of the sequence; with VIX 14.89, flat yields and WTI down 1.53%, Tail eases to 15 and Stress to 46
body:
The observation that changes this hour is that the overnight extension sequence has finally produced a retracement. Yahoo Finance shows NQ at 29,228.75, up 123.00 points or 0.42% on the 29,105.75 settle, with the overnight band at 29,017.00-29,290.25; Investing.com independently shows 29,237.75, up 132.00 points or 0.45%, on a delayed stamp. The 29,290.25 print is a sixth higher extreme, but only two points above the 29,288.25 high recorded an hour ago, and price has since given back roughly 60 points from it. An hour ago NQ was holding within eleven points of its extreme; it is now about 0.21% below it, having retraced close to 22% of the whole overnight range. Repeated extension while holding near the extreme was the structure that carried Tail up to 17; a marginal new high that fails to hold, followed by a visible pullback, is the structure that reverses it. Tail eases to 15.

The cross-asset backdrop is unchanged to marginally friendlier. VIX is 14.89, down 6.00% from a 15.84 close. Treasury yields are effectively flat with a slight upward drift: 2Y 4.25% (+2bp), 10Y 4.71% (+1bp), 30Y 5.24%. Crude has extended Monday's decline, with WTI at $83.705, down 1.53%, and Brent at $90.85, down 1.23%. That oil path matters for the geopolitical channel: the US rolled out a global sanctions programme focused on Iran on Monday, and rather than pricing a supply disruption, crude has fallen for a second session while European equities rebounded. Falling oil on an escalatory headline is the market removing an energy-shock premium, not adding one.

European cash confirms the tone for a second hour. The ifo Business Climate Index for Germany was released at 10:00 Berlin time and came in above expectations, against a consensus that had looked for a decline; Stoxx 600 is around +0.4% with DAX and CAC 40 both above +0.4%. Delayed latest-session context shows the advance is tech-led and narrow: NQ futures +0.39% against ES +0.15% and YM +0.06%, semiconductors positive across all seven tracked names with a mean of +1.60%, but megacaps mixed at six of eight positive with AAPL -0.24% and MSFT -0.17%. That is a rotation into semiconductors ahead of the Nvidia report, not a broad index impulse, and the 0.94% overnight range is consistent with a grind.

Stress eases marginally to 46 because the retracement removes some of the mean-reversion-failure premium, while the afternoon calendar keeps it in the elevated band: Barkin at 12:00Z, weekly ADP at 12:15Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, the cash open at 13:30Z and a three-release cluster at 14:00Z. Confidence rises to 88 on two agreeing price feeds, freshly verified yields and crude, a verified macro release inside the hour and shared context collected two minutes before this assessment. The dominant catalysts sit just beyond the forecast horizon: Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and Durable Goods at 12:30Z on 26 August, with Nvidia reporting after that session's close.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 08:00Z on 24 August with Tail 17 and Stress 55 in a trend-down mode, which collapsed to 12 within an hour and held an 11 to 13 band through the European session. The only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, mapping to WATCH, and the peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That episode resolved in a single hour, falling to 13 by 15:00Z and to a floor of 7 by 21:00Z, which is the pattern the calibration expects when an event repricing is orderly. The overnight hours ran 8 to 12 in mixed and normal modes until 04:00Z, when the mode turned to trend-up and Tail began a steady four-hour climb through 13, 14 and 15 to 17 at 07:00Z as successive higher extremes accumulated. Stress spent the whole window between 42 and 60 and Confidence between 80 and 88, so evidence quality was never the constraint.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 15 on the observed failure of the sixth extreme and the first meaningful pullback of the overnight sequence, holds 15 through the European morning and eases to 14 in the calendar-empty hours before the US day. The series rebuilds to 15 at 12:00Z for the Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 17 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the cash open follows at 13:30Z, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z for the three-release cluster, which is also the centre of the 13:30Z to 14:30Z danger window. It decays through 18 and 16 across the afternoon, steps back to 16 at 20:00Z where the cash close overlaps a second Barkin appearance, then falls to a floor of 11 in the thin pre-Asia hours. The final stretch rebuilds gently from 11 to 15 as Asia opens and Europe approaches Core PCE day, on calendar structure rather than observed price path. Stress follows the same shape between 40 and 57, and Confidence decays from 88 to 66 purely as a function of evidence age.
